question.prompt: What is the sum of the digits of the smallest prime that can be written as a sum of \(5\) distinct primes?

solutions.title: Find the smallest odd-prime sums
solutions.explanation:
The prime \(2\) cannot be included: the other four distinct primes would be odd, making the sum even and greater than \(2\), hence composite.

The five smallest odd primes give the smallest possible sum:
\[
3+5+7+11+13=39=3\cdot13,
\]
which is not prime. Any different selection must contain a prime at least \(17\). Its other four primes sum to at least \(3+5+7+11=26\), so every different selection has sum at least \(43\).

That bound is achieved by
\[
3+5+7+11+17=43.
\]
Since \(\sqrt{43}<7\), checking the possible prime divisors \(2,3,5\) suffices to establish primality. None divides \(43\), so \(43\) is the smallest prime obtainable.

Its digit sum is \(4+3=\boxed{7}\), choice \(\text{B}\).
